note: The single obfuscation pass U13 runs over the bundled, minified game (KTD4).
`options` is handed to javascript-obfuscator untouched; `rationale` carries one
line per option saying why it is set, including the four that are set to their
default value on purpose. `tests/unit/obfuscated-build.test.ts` fails if the two
objects stop naming exactly the same keys, so an option cannot be added here
without a reader ever being told why it is on.
The goal this serves is stated once, in the plan: the shipped file should be hard
for a reading agent to reconstruct into intelligible source. It is not a claim
about the data, which ships as plain JSON next to it by design and is the more

rationale.target: The output runs in a browser from a file:// URL; there is no Node flavour of this build.
rationale.seed: Pinned so two builds of one tree are byte-identical, which is what lets the deploy publish the artifact CI tested instead of rebuilding it (KTD18). An arbitrary constant, deliberately not a version or a date: bumping it would invalidate every cached copy for no gain.
rationale.compact: One line, no formatting to read — and selfDefending only works on compact output.
rationale.simplify: Default. Left on because it folds the expressions the other transforms generate; turning it off makes the output larger without making it harder to read.
rationale.identifierNamesGenerator: Short mangled names rather than the hexadecimal default, and shuffled so the order they are handed out in carries no trace of declaration order. Measured: hexadecimal produces 3.5 MB of _0x1a2b3c where this produces 1.9 MB, and a name nobody can bind to a meaning is no more readable for being longer.
rationale.renameGlobals: Off. The bundle is one IIFE and declares no globals of its own; the names it does read — window, document, Intl — are the platform's and renaming them would break the page.
rationale.renameProperties: Off. The engine reads its data by property name (byCode, CURRENCY_UNITS, SPECIAL_CAPITALS) and the shell reads the DOM by API name; renaming properties would break both, and the safe mode only narrows the damage rather than preventing it.
rationale.transformObjectKeys: Off, deliberately, per the plan. The engine reads CURRENCY_UNITS, SPECIAL_CAPITALS and byCode by a country code computed at runtime, and this transform rewrites exactly those literals. A table of that shape does survive it in isolation — that was measured, so this is a precaution rather than a demonstrated break — but the tables are built and read in more places than a synthetic check covers, and reworking them to suit the obfuscator is the wrong trade for a transform that mostly adds size. renameProperties, next to it, does break the same read.
rationale.controlFlowFlattening: The transform that actually defeats reconstruction: straight-line logic becomes a dispatch loop over a shuffled switch, so the order of the source is no longer in the output.
rationale.controlFlowFlatteningThreshold: 0.75 of eligible blocks, the default. Measured: 1.0 adds 116 KB for the last quarter of an effect already achieved, and this transform is where nearly all of the hot-path cost recorded in tests/browser/obfuscated-build.spec.ts comes from.
rationale.deadCodeInjection: Adds unreachable branches built from the real code, so a reader cannot tell which half runs. This is what makes the flattened dispatch expensive to unpick rather than merely tedious.
rationale.deadCodeInjectionThreshold: 0.4, the default. Higher mostly buys file size: the injected branches are copies of real ones, so each one costs what it duplicates.
rationale.numbersToExpressions: Turns literal constants into arithmetic. Aimed at the globe and the scoring, where a bare 0.5 or 1000 is the fastest way to recognise what a function computes.
rationale.stringArray: The prerequisite for the rest: every literal moves into one table and every use becomes an index into it.
rationale.stringArrayEncoding: RC4 rather than base64: base64 is reversible by eye, RC4 needs the key and the decoder. Affordable only because the flag payload is not in this table — see splitStringsChunkLength. The boot cost was not modelled but measured: tests/browser/obfuscated-build.spec.ts opens the published file and reaches a playable question, and the arrival flight is unchanged.
rationale.stringArrayThreshold: 1 — every string, not the default three-quarters. A quarter of the literals left in place is a quarter of the catalog, the question templates and the error messages still readable, which is most of what names the code.
rationale.stringArrayCallsTransform: Moves the array lookups themselves behind generated functions, so the call sites do not all share one recognisable shape.
rationale.stringArrayIndexShift: Adds a constant offset to every index, so an index read out of the output does not address the entry it appears to.
rationale.stringArrayRotate: Rotates the table at load behind a self-checking loop, so the table as it appears in the file is not the table at runtime.
rationale.stringArrayShuffle: Shuffles the table, so entry order carries no trace of source order. Seeded, so it is the same shuffle every build.
rationale.stringArrayWrappersType: Function wrappers rather than plain variables: a variable alias is one substitution away from being inlined back.
rationale.stringArrayWrappersCount: 5 per scope. Enough that no single wrapper accounts for most reads, which is what a reader looks for first.
rationale.stringArrayWrappersChainedCalls: Wrappers call wrappers, so resolving one does not resolve the scope.
rationale.stringArrayWrappersParametersMaxCount: 5, which lets the generated wrappers differ in arity as well as in name.
rationale.splitStrings: Breaks the literals that survive into concatenated fragments, so a grep for a message finds nothing.
rationale.splitStringsChunkLength: 5. This is the setting KTD6 warns must never reach the 1.5 MB flag payload — at five characters a chunk that blob would become roughly 380,000 fragments. It is safe here only because the flags are inlined as their own plain JSON block and never enter the bundle.
rationale.selfDefending: Makes the output break rather than degrade if it is reformatted. This is why obfuscation is the last step: nothing may touch the JavaScript afterwards, which is also why the published directory needs .nojekyll.
rationale.debugProtection: Off, deliberately. It can freeze the browser when DevTools opens, and it defends against a reader watching the code run rather than against one reconstructing it — which is not the goal here.
rationale.disableConsoleOutput: Off, deliberately. The browser suite fails the build on a console error; swallowing console output would hide real breakage in exchange for nothing an attacker cannot recover.
rationale.unicodeEscapeSequence: Off. The catalog is Czech and English; escaping every accented letter would inflate the file to hide text that is on screen anyway.
